title: Counterfactual legal tests are analysis, not authority
summary: Legal Effect can evaluate explicit hypothetical assumptions and compare outcomes, but a counterfactual is labelled analysis. It cannot be laundered into authoritative legal effect or publication evidence merely because the model or engine can calculate it.
invariants: Counterfactual assumptions must be explicit and provenance-bound.
Counterfactual outputs remain non-authoritative unless separately established through the real evidence/compiler path.
A hypothetical comparison cannot create or waive an entitlement.
Historical evaluation must distinguish event/effective time from evaluation time.

provenance.claim: Legal Effect v0.14 owns structured legal-effect evaluation and the compiler/certification authority boundary; public legal API remains legal.effect/0.10.
